title: Public Works Construction Contract: Larkmoor Community Center Renovation and Seismic Upgrade
fictional_notice: All parties and facts are invented.

defects.title: Progress payments due in 75 days with no interest
defects.why: Section 5.2 allows City 75 days to pay an undisputed, properly submitted Payment Request and says amounts paid in that period bear no interest. A local agency that does not pay within 30 days of receipt owes interest at the legal rate.
quotes: Payment of each undisputed progress payment shall be made within seventy-five (75) days after the City's receipt of a properly submitted Payment Request. Amounts paid within that period shall not bear interest.

defects.title: Prevailing wage carve-out for demolition, site, landscape and cleaning labor
defects.why: Section 6.2 says prevailing wage law does not apply to demolition, site clearing, landscaping and final cleaning labor and lets Contractor set those wage rates. Prevailing wages must be paid to workers on a public work over $1,000, and this is an $8,415,000 public project.
quotes: Labor for demolition, site clearing, landscaping and final cleaning is not subject to prevailing wage law, and Contractor may set the wage rates for those classifications at its discretion.

defects.title: Registration exemption for subcontracts under $250,000
defects.why: Section 6.4 exempts Subcontractors with subcontracts under $250,000 from registration with the Department of Industrial Relations. No contractor or subcontractor may work on a public work unless registered, and the only size exemption is for projects of $25,000 or less ($15,000 or less for maintenance).
quotes: The registration requirement of this Section does not apply to any Subcontractor whose subcontract price is less than Two Hundred Fifty Thousand Dollars ($250,000), and Contractor may engage such Subcontractors without regard to their registration status.

defects.title: Apprenticeship rules limited to subcontracts over $500,000
defects.why: Section 6.6 applies the apprenticeship requirements only to Contractor and to Subcontractors with subcontracts over $500,000. The statutory exemption reaches only contracts of general contractors, or of specialty contractors not bidding through a general, that involve less than $30,000.
quotes: The apprenticeship requirements of Labor Code section 1777.5 shall apply only to Contractor and to Subcontractors whose subcontracts exceed Five Hundred Thousand Dollars ($500,000); all other Subcontractors are exempt from employing apprentices and from making training fund contributions.

defects.title: Subcontractor listing only above 3 percent of the bid
defects.why: Section 7.1 requires listing only of Subcontractors performing more than 3 percent of the total Bid. The prime must list each subcontractor doing work worth more than one-half of 1 percent of the prime's total bid.
quotes: Contractor's Bid listed, and Contractor is required to identify, only those Subcontractors performing work in an amount in excess of three percent (3%) of Contractor's total Bid.

defects.title: Payment bond waived
defects.why: Section 9.2 waives the payment bond. A payment bond of not less than 100 percent of the contract price is required before work starts on a public works contract over $25,000.
quotes: In consideration of Contractor's financial strength and the retention held under Article 5, the City waives the requirement of a payment bond for this Project, and Contractor shall not be required to furnish one.

defects.title: Indemnity for City's active negligence
defects.why: Section 9.5 makes Contractor indemnify City for Claims arising from City's active negligence, excepting only sole willful misconduct. A clause in a construction contract with a public agency that makes the contractor liable for the agency's active negligence is void.
quotes: including Claims arising from the active or passive negligence of the City or any other Indemnitee, excepting only Claims caused by the sole willful misconduct of the City

defects.title: Retention released 120 days after completion with no late charge
defects.why: Section 11.4 holds retention for 120 days after completion and bars any interest or charge. Retention must be released within 60 days after completion, and late payment carries a charge of 2 percent per month.
quotes: The City shall release the retention, less amounts withheld under this Contract, one hundred twenty (120) days after the date of completion of the Work, and no interest or charge shall accrue on retention held during that period.
